acceptance: `policy.plan_review` (default off) validates against orchestration.schema.json and takes `mode` (off, advisory or required), `lenses` (built-in checklists item, alignment, security, testability and gui-api shipped as data under specy_road/orchestration/plan_lenses/; a project may replace a lens's rows or add a lens) and `routing` (per lens, zone globs and title/acceptance keywords; item and testability apply to every leaf; alignment runs once per milestone or batch plan over the set, never per leaf); with off, pickup and `review delegate` behave as before

Stage (a): the planner explicitly runs `review delegate` in plan mode with leaf ids or a milestone id (no automatic run from CRUD commands or hooks); it reuses the roster pick, distinct families and fresh bare sessions, and gives reviewers the routed lenses' rows plus the leaves' sheet, acceptance, zones, dependencies and ancestor context; every finding carries a `lens` tag and a row id; records are plan-prefixed files (PLAN-REVIEW-<model>.md) under work/reviews/<ID>/ against a separate plan-review schema, never count toward code-review approval, and hold a fingerprint the filing command computes (SHA-256 of canonical acceptance, touch_zones, dependencies and sheet text) plus the integration commit; the planner answers each finding on the record with `amended` or `not a defect because <reason>`

Stage (b) at pickup is deterministic and checks four conditions: the fingerprint differs; a dependency that was not Complete at review time is Complete and git diff --name-only from the stored commit to the current integration commit intersects the leaf's zones (undetermined, with a warning, if either commit is unavailable); a zone matches no tracked file; a finding is unanswered. Advisory: all four warn and pickup proceeds. Required: no plan record at the current fingerprint, or an unanswered finding, excludes the leaf in do_next_task.py; the dependency and zone conditions only warn in every mode. No lens is required by this leaf; a later M20 posture may mark lenses required; routing is built so that a later M20 risk label can be one more routing input alongside zones and keywords (no labels in this leaf)

Tests with a stub reviewer and no network: a vague fixture leaf gets item rows flagged (uncheckable line, contradicting lines, named file outside zones, unbounded detection rule) and a clear one gets none; table-driven routing rows (a guard or review-record zone routes security, a gui_app_* zone routes gui-api, every leaf gets item and testability, alignment only on a milestone or batch run); a project override replaces a built-in lens row; each stage (b) condition warns, including a sheet-only edit; required refuses on a missing or stale record and on an unanswered finding but not on the dependency or zone conditions; plan records do not satisfy code-review approval; off is a no-op; docs/orchestration-review.md documents lenses, routing and both stages

The built-in item lens carries the row 'a new value stored in a schema-validated record (a flag, enum or status value) names that schema file in the touch zones'; a fixture leaf that adds a worker flag without specy_road/schemas/worker-record.schema.json in its zones gets that row flagged (2026-11-05: M22.5 passed two plan reviews, then its worker stopped for that schema)
nodes.title: Plan review after planning, and a staleness check before pickup

acceptance: orchestrate plan walks active preferences in active_preferences order and each one's models in stored order: for its role, the first model that passes check_assignment moves to the front of that role's candidates, and counts as applied only when the existing picker then assigns it (no slot is added past reviewers_required). Text prints 'applied <pref id>: <model> as <role> on <leaf>' only for assigned models, and --json preferences_applied holds those {id, model, role, leaf} objects

A preference applied on no leaf stays under preferences_not_applied with the first reason among applies_to set, no role, no models, not rostered, unavailable, ineligible: <first refusal>, superseded by <pref id> and policy-constrained (eligible but displaced by independence, distinct families, strong review or the slot count); with no active preference, text and --json match today's plan; --spread round-robins the capable executors after the preferred one is first

Reviewer selection is one function of a node, the roster and the ledger: orchestrate plan calls it per ready leaf, and review delegate calls it for resolve_target's node even when that node is active and absent from parallel_batches, using its recorded executor. Without --model, review delegate launches the first selected reviewer with no gate-accepted record at the commit --ref names (default the registered branch tip); when every selected reviewer has one it prints that no reviewer remains and exits 0; an empty selection exits 2; both launch nothing. With --model the launch is unchanged plus one stdout notice when the selection's reviewer differs; --resume and a target that is not a roadmap node still require --model

Stub-harness CLI tests with time frozen and --retries 0: the preferred model is the leaf's executor, outside may_process, unavailable, or blocked by distinct families, and strong review with a satisfying model each refuse or select the legal alternative before any harness launch marker; a REVIEW-*.md that is malformed, for another commit, or not gate-accepted by the gate's own check does not count as filed. coordinator_decision_lines and specyrd-orchestrate.md say which preferences the plan applies and that the coordinator applies the rest
